claim: Blending is described as a network: two inputs, a generic space of shared structure, a cross-space mapping, and a blend built by composition, completion and elaboration (running the blend). The founding paper is a descriptive model with no experiment.
agent_test: Prompt the agent to emit input A, input B, generic space, mapping, selective projection list, blend, then run the blend; compare with plain analogy prompting at equal tokens on cross-domain design and puzzle items.

claim: Selective projection is part of the model: the blend drops most input detail (calendar date, language, being dead). Only the authors' hand-picked cases show this; no test of whether dropping detail improves outcomes.
agent_test: Ablate an explicit 'what NOT to carry over' step; measure the rate of incoherent or contradictory blends by blind grading.

claim: The Buddhist monk riddle is solved by fusing the two days onto one path so two walkers meet. No solve rate with or without the blend frame was found in the sources. Gap search (second pass, several searches): still no solve-rate study found for people or models.
agent_test: Run monk-style same-path isomorphs with and without a 'put both on one path' step at equal tokens.

claim: Blending theory is hard to falsify as stated. Critics (Gibbs 2000, Ritchie 2004, Glebkin 2013) say it describes but does not predict; governing principles were added in reply but their use in practice is unclear.
agent_test: Do not claim blend-step gains from theory fit; require a measured ablation (blend step on/off) for every use.

claim: N400 amplitude rises from literal to literal-mapping to metaphor sentences (N=18; linear trend over 98% of condition variance), but literal mapping did not differ significantly from either neighbour. Consistent with graded integration cost; does not separate blending from cloze or salience accounts. The two agent records read the same paper.
agent_test: Not a direct agent test; if used, treat 'harder mappings cost more' as a prior for allocating compute to far blends.

claim: Semantically odd blends (privative 'fake X') cost human accuracy (N=36, pre-registered MEG/EEG study; privative vs subsective p<.0001). The cost may come from negation or type-shifting, not blending, so it supports blending only weakly.
agent_test: Skip as an agent test; note the rival explanations when citing.

claim: No large-sample replication, meta-analysis, or direct failed replication of a blending-specific prediction was found. Human studies are small (N=10 to 36 for lab and tool studies; N=100 for one rating study).
agent_test: Treat every effect as a hypothesis; replicate on our own agent with several seeds.

claim: LLMs do worse at blending than at association or analogy: over 35 models a valid blend 43.4%, analogy 53.4%, association 59.0%; humans (Prolific, N=75, 5 items per task, skipped scored zero) 12.8%, 32.9%, 22.1%. One preprint, LLM-judged (75% agreement with humans on unanimous items).
agent_test: Run our agent on the KOMBINE-style blending task, unaided vs scaffolded, with a human-graded subset.

claim: Abstraction bottleneck in blending: models find a valid generic space only 43.4% of the time, but given one describe a coherent blend 97.1% of the time. The 43.4% equals the valid-blend rate, so it is one number, not two findings.
agent_test: Add a propose-then-check generic-space step; measure the valid-generic-space rate with and without it at equal tokens.

claim: An explicit abstraction or schema step before mapping or transfer helps downstream quality in two independent AI settings: narrative analogy (Qwen 0.17 to 0.46, Llama 0.16 to 0.45 on a 4-way MCQ) and visual metaphor transfer (human ratings fall from 4.47/4.56/4.51 to 4.01/3.71/3.83 on the first three scales when the transfer agent is removed). Both are authors' own ablations, not at equal compute; the narrative result uses a cosine mapper, and LLM chain of thought alone scored 0.41.
agent_test: Same items, abstraction step on/off, token budget matched; report the gain against plain chain of thought, not against a weak mapper.

claim: Different LLMs invent the same blends: 19.9% (412/2,070) of invented concepts reuse a property invented by another model at the loosest threshold; blends repeat 14.3 times more than analogies at k=2 (37.3% vs 2.6%); same-provider pairs 2.3 times more likely.
agent_test: Sample the blend step many times with varied inputs; measure property overlap; test if forced input variation lowers repeats.

claim: LLM-assisted blending tools help people produce more ideas and feel less strain: PopBlends 2.03 vs 0.87 ideas per pair (N=10, p<0.001, mental demand 2.85 vs 5.80), Creative Blends (N=24, SUS d=.80), Scideator (N=22, CSI median 70.5 vs 61.0). Gains in rated newness were small (Scideator 0.5 on a 7-point scale). All are the authors' own systems against baselines, with self-report measures.
agent_test: Count distinct, expert-graded ideas per token for blend step vs plain brainstorming; do not use self-report.

claim: About 56% of single LLM blend suggestions are judged good (PopBlends: 56.0/55.3/58.7% by strategy, kappa .43 to .48), but 90 to 97% of pairs have at least one good suggestion among five. Generating several and selecting pays off more than trusting one.
agent_test: Compare best-of-5 with a judge-selected single blend vs one blend at equal tokens.

claim: Which text-to-image blending method is best depends on the pair type and the panel. Olearo 2024 (23 people, 24 pairs): SWITCH 2.26, TEXTUAL 2.54, ALTERNATE 2.61, UNET 2.68 mean rank, TEXTUAL best on animals (1.98). Olearo 2025 (N=100): alternate/switch preferred over textual (0.60 to 0.61). Rank gaps are small.
agent_test: Not applicable to a text agent; cite only as a warning that method ranking flips by category.

claim: In diffusion models a true blend appears mainly in the middle of a text-embedding interpolation: blended-concept depiction 0.621 at the midpoint but 0.389 averaged over 9 ratios (1,000 images); one concept dominates away from the midpoint.
agent_test: Not an agent test; supports 'do not average inputs, choose a projection'.

claim: Early masked language models predicted object properties from similes far better than ConceptNet (precision at 1000: 66.38 best vs 5.90), so language models can supply the property step of a blend. The table is garbled and the models are pre-instruction-tuning.
agent_test: Ask the agent for properties of each input before mapping; check property precision against a gold list.

claim: Vision-language models rival humans at understanding visual mashups (implication winning rate: experts 78.3%, GPT-4o 73.5%, average humans 51.0%, Claude-3.5-Sonnet 62.9%); an explanation-level prompt had mean rank 1.98 vs 2.40 for the version without it; fusion mashups are identified better than replacement ones. The judge may be GPT-4o (own-model bias).
agent_test: Test 'explain shared attributes first' on text blends at equal tokens.

claim: Student physics reasoning shows blends with inertia: a single-scope blend (math with physics) tends to persist until new evidence or a prompt moves it (answer 47,500 s stood until simple numbers cued the physical input). Qualitative case studies, no frequencies.
agent_test: Check if the agent keeps a wrong blend after contrary evidence; test a forced 're-blend' trigger.

claim: The conceptual papers on LLM blending (Sato 2025, Lynn 2026) contain no measurements; claims that fusing incompatible domains raises hallucination are untested in the text read.
agent_test: Run a controlled test: compatible vs incompatible domain fusion prompts, blind-graded errors, several seeds.

claim: An explicit blending-theory schema (relational invariant, transfer step, diagnostic step) beat a strong single-prompt baseline on visual metaphor transfer in human ratings (N=100): removing the diagnostic agent cut visual appeal from 4.51 to 3.98. Authors' own ablation, advertising images only.
agent_test: Port to text: generic space + transfer + diagnosis vs single prompt, equal tokens.

claim: No study was found that tests an explicit generic-space or blend step against plain chain of thought on a reasoning task at equal tokens. The nearest tests (Beyond Pixels, YARN, Scideator) change compute and domain. Second gap search (arXiv, web, listings) also found none.
agent_test: This is our main test: blend step vs chain of thought on puzzles and design tasks, token-matched.

claim: Combinational creativity tools can raise diversity without quality evidence: the harmony-blending tool (N=25) gave more unexpected output with no independent quality rating; Misty (14 developers) showed 103 blending operations and satisfaction 3.2/5 with no control.
agent_test: Rate novelty and usefulness separately; do not take diversity as quality.

claim: LLMs regress toward the mean in creative advertising ideas (over 1,000 ideas, Galton's Law of Mediocrity); effect sizes were not extracted, so only the direction is recorded.
agent_test: Compare idea spread of the blend step against plain sampling at equal tokens.

claim: Counterfactual comprehension studies do not contradict the order composition, completion, elaboration. de Vega 2007 (3 experiments) shows the as-if space is briefly held then suppressed. Ferguson and Sanford 2008 (3 eye-tracking experiments, N=36 each) shows real-world knowledge still disrupts early reading inside a counterfactual context, supporting a dual, two-stage process. Neither tests blend operation order; the earlier claim came second hand.
agent_test: Check each blend against real-world constraints before accepting it; drop the as-if space once the question is answered.

claim: LLM judging of blend and creativity quality is only partly reliable. Vibe Spaces: an LLM judge matches the human top-1 blend 35.7% and 31.3% of the time (25% chance), top-2 55.1% and 51.8%; human-human kappa between raters is just 0.15 to 0.33. Short-story judging: LLM judges agree with each other (ICC .86-.94) but with humans only ICC .43.
agent_test: Grade a blind human slice of hard blends and report kappa for any LLM judge used on blend validity.

claim: A step that first finds the relevant shared attributes of two inputs (a generic-space-like step) is the common element of tools that humans rate better: Vibe Spaces (image blends rated more creative and coherent than GPT and Gemini) and, per a press release only, VisiBlends (96% vs 21% success). No matched ablation against plain prompting at equal cost is read in text.
agent_test: Run generic-space-first vs direct blend vs chain of thought at equal tokens on design and puzzle items, human-graded.

claim: Computational blending frameworks (Eppe 2018 with answer set programming, Divago) report proof-of-concept demonstrations in math, music and creature invention, not controlled comparisons with non-blending baselines.
agent_test: Do not cite classic systems as evidence of benefit.

claim: No failed replication and no controlled blending versus relevance theory test was found for noun-noun compounds or mixed metaphors in two passes; the debate remains theoretical (Sabzevari 2011 chapter is the closest pointer).
agent_test: none
